Executibe Order

EXEMPTION oF GrorGE G. Hepa@cockK rrom COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FOR AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404;
5 U.S. C., sec. 692b), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch
or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the
District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for auto-
matic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued
in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the con-
trary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive order, exempt from the
provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so
requires: * * * ”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that George G. Hedgcock, senior
pathologist in the Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture, who was
exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order
No. 6338, dated October 14, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this
section and continued in the service until November 1, 1935;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid
section, I do hereby exempt George G. Hedgcock from the provisions thereof and
continue him in the service until November 1, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT.
Tue Waite House,
September 30, 1934.

(No. 6862]

U. S$, GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 19346

Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF GEORGE G. HEpGcock From Compu.sory RETIREMENT
FOR AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C.,
sec. 715a), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or
service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District
of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic
separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such
service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided,
That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this
section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that George G. Hedgecock, senior
pathologist, Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture, who was exempted
from compulsory retirement for periods totaling three years and eight months by
Executive Orders No. 6338 of October 14, 1933, No. 6862 of September 30, 1934, No.
7208 of October 19, 1935, and No. 7475 of October 19, 1936, be further exempted from
the provisions of this section and continued in the service until January 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt George G. Hedgcock from the provisions
thereof and continue him in the service until January 1, 1938.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
Tue Waite Hovss,
June 24, 1937.

[No. 7645]

U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1997
